result: In 37 medication-free CDC-defined CFS patients without psychiatric comorbidity vs 28 controls, 24-h urinary free cortisol was lower in CFS; baseline cortisol was raised only before the hCRH test, and low-dose hydrocortisone raised UFC.
reason: Independent cohort, same measure (24-h UFC), same direction; not among finding_studies.

result: ACTH responses to hCRH, insulin stress and D-fenfluramine were normal, but cortisol responses to hCRH and D-fenfluramine were lower once ACTH was controlled, pointing to reduced adrenal output; responders to hydrocortisone showed reversal of the blunted cortisol response to hCRH.
reason: Shows blunted adrenal cortisol output relative to endogenous ACTH (CRH challenge, ACTH-adjusted), not a direct ACTH stimulation or glucocorticoid suppression test, so it extends rather than replicates.

result: In 22 monozygotic twin pairs discordant for CFS, resting 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT showed no difference in visually read abnormalities or quantified rCBF, unchanged after adjusting for fitness, depression and mood.
reason: Same measure (resting SPECT rCBF), null result in a well-matched co-twin design; not among finding_studies.

result: 24-h urinary free cortisol was significantly lower in 121 CFS clinic patients than 64 controls, regardless of psychiatric comorbidity, and was unrelated to medication use, sleep disturbance or disability.
reason: Independent cohort, same measure (24-h UFC), same direction; addresses some confounders the finding raises.

result: In 7 CFS patients vs 7 matched controls, prolonged standing produced excessive delayed (usually after 10 min) orthostatic hypotension, and foot-vein contractile compliance to IV norepinephrine was reduced, implying impaired sympathetic venous innervation and leg venous pooling.
reason: Specific measured result (pedal vein compliance, delayed OH) not covered by the atlas; autonomic/vascular domain. Very small n.

result: In 19 CFS patients vs 19 matched controls, a 1-h arginine vasopressin infusion produced a reduced ACTH response and a more rapid cortisol response in CFS, interpreted as reduced hypothalamic CRH secretion.
reason: Measures pituitary ACTH response to AVP as a proxy for central CRH drive, not adrenal response to ACTH or glucocorticoid suppression; the faster cortisol rise does not fit blunted adrenal response; no atlas finding on central CRH hypofunction.

result: Basal hormones were normal; 4 min after maximal treadmill exercise ACTH, epinephrine, prolactin and TSH responses were lower in CFS than sedentary controls, GH response possibly exaggerated, norepinephrine similar, and no differences the next day.
reason: Exercise-induced pituitary/adrenomedullary hormone responses, not cortisol response to ACTH or glucocorticoid suppression; no atlas finding covers post-exercise neuroendocrine responses (GH signal too tentative for endocrine-gh-igf1).

result: Among 29 CFS, 24 MS, 23 depressed and 25 control participants, groups differed in memory, language and spatial ability, and after covarying for depression patient groups still differed from controls mainly in memory.
reason: Neuropsychological battery shows cognitive (memory) deficits in CFS not explained by depression, same direction as the finding; small sample.

result: With 4-hourly sampling over 24 h in 36 CFS patients and 20 controls, circadian rhythms of PRL, TSH, ACTH and cortisol were preserved, but ACTH was lower at 24:00 and 04:00 (p<0.001) and PRL higher at 04:00 in CFS.
reason: Basal diurnal ACTH/prolactin profile, not a challenge test; cortisol was not reported as different, so it does not fit low-cortisol either; no atlas finding on nocturnal ACTH.

result: In 20 CFS patients vs 20 matched neighbourhood controls on an incremental maximal exercise test, physical fitness (actual vs predicted workload/heart-rate ratio) did not differ, 9 patients were fitter than their control, and more patients than controls did not reach a physiological limit.
reason: Supports the finding's conclusion by a different design (patients not less fit than matched controls) rather than the same measure; it also bears against muscle-exertion-low-peak-vo2.
